ref: Check for urgent abnormal thoughts or behaviour conditions / all rules (trigger)
text: Every rule is anchored on (or Abnormal behavior, Disturbance in thinking), but neither concept is a common symptom or warning sign per the house standard, and the natural warning-sign entry point, Aggressive behavior, is NOT a SNOMED descendant of Abnormal behavior (checked with is_a), nor are Hallucinations a descendant of Disturbance in thinking. Unless the VHA intake records one of these two concepts, nothing fires on this page. Needs a remaining-questions note and ideally an extra trigger (e.g. Aggressive behavior, or a broad possible pre-screen as on the gold page).

ref: Urgent: abnormal thoughts or behaviour of sudden or recent onset
text: The six 'likely' diagnoses (delirium, mania, psychosis, stimulant intoxication, alcohol intoxication, withdrawal, poisoning) sit inside the red box under 'Manage urgently', yet the priority rule fires only on the Sudden/Recent onset qualifiers. A patient recorded with Abnormal behavior (no onset qualifier) + Fluctuation of level of consciousness + temperature 39 gets probable Delirium but no Urgent priority. The house standard says to reference (active_condition X) for likely diagnoses named in the red box; adding the seven active_condition alternates to the priority rule's 'or' would close this.

ref: Diagnose probable stimulant drug intoxication in abnormal thoughts or behaviour
text: The comma list is encoded as a flat 'or', so a single non-specific finding (Nausea, which is a common symptom; Sweating; Restlessness; or a BP of 140/90 alone) plus abnormal behaviour yields a PROBABLE stimulant intoxication. Nausea, Sweating and Restlessness are also withdrawal findings, so the same patient is simultaneously probable withdrawal if any stopped/decreased finding is present. The page shows a cluster; any2 (available in the language) would be a more faithful reading. The same flat-'or' choice in the mania and alcohol-intoxication rules is less harmful because those findings are specific.

ref: Diagnose probable stimulant drug intoxication in abnormal thoughts or behaviour
text: The page box is a comma list with no conjunction ('Dilated pupils, restlessness, paranoia, nausea, sweating, pulse >= 100, BP >= 140/90'), presented as a clinical picture. Encoding it as a flat 'or' means nausea alone, sweating alone or restlessness alone with abnormal behaviour yields probable stimulant intoxication, and those same findings also sit in the withdrawal rule. The page's reading is not certain, but 'or' is the loosest possible one; 'any2' (or dilated pupils/paranoia plus one other) is closer to 'likely'. Also 'Pulse, function' should be 'Heart rate'. 'BP >= 140/90' as systolic >= 140 or diastolic >= 90 follows the gold file's convention and is fine.
